query: Why do some travel expenses get declined, and which factors contribute the most?

per_column.name: is_travel
per_column.rationale: Flags travel expenses, the candidate cause whose effect on declination the query directly asks about ('some travel expenses get declined').

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: Presence of a source_id is a data-completeness/provenance indicator; not a plausible common cause of both travel status and declination, more a bookkeeping artifact.

per_column.name: is_unfinalized
per_column.rationale: Being unfinalized is likely part of the processing pathway toward a decline decision (on the causal path), so it functions as a mediator/near-collider rather than a confounder.

per_column.name: amount_range
per_column.rationale: Expense amount plausibly influences whether an expense is travel-related (travel tends to be costlier) and independently drives scrutiny/declination, making it a genuine common cause surfaced from data.

per_column.name: has_processed_date
per_column.rationale: Whether a processed date exists is downstream of the decision outcome/processing, not a prior common cause; conditioning on it risks collider bias.

per_column.name: days_to_process
per_column.rationale: Processing duration is realized during handling of the expense and lies on the path to the outcome; it is a mediator/consequence, not a pre-treatment confounder.

per_column.name: is_cust_support_travel
per_column.rationale: A narrow subcategory of travel; overlaps with the treatment definition rather than serving as an independent common cause of both treatment and outcome.

judge.rationale: A treatment is clearly present (is_travel), matching the query's focus on travel expenses. However, the causal-estimation scaffolding is weak: only amount_range qualifies as a plausible common cause of both being a travel expense and being declined, and even that is modest. The remaining added columns are dominated by mediators/consequences of processing (is_unfinalized, days_to_process), colliders/outcome-adjacent completeness flags (has_processed_date, has_source_id), or restatements of the treatment (is_cust_support_travel). Adjusting for these would introduce mediator/collider bias rather than removing confounding. Thus the system did surface one genuine, non-query-named confounder, but failed to assemble a credible confounder set, so it only partially realizes the causal-attribution claim.
